# Purpose

This notebook evaluates the initial repeatability and accuracy of `INS-0002`, the first registered Kepler quadrant, using the known geometry of Quadrant Calibration 001.

The analysis preserves the reconciled working observations unchanged. Ideal angles, residuals, summaries, and diagnostic flags are derived only within this analysis.

# Executed protocol

The preliminary campaign design used three elevated targets at a longer observing distance. During execution, the observer deliberately expanded the angular range by:

- sitting rather than standing;
- moving to a horizontal distance of 48 inches from the calibration range; and
- marking five elevated targets at independently measured 12-inch intervals above the eye-level reference.

This is treated as an intentional protocol improvement, not as a defect. The executed geometry recorded in `calibration_geometry.yaml` is authoritative for this analysis.

```{julia}
using CSV
using DataFrames
using YAML
using Statistics

```

# Paths

The paths below assume this notebook remains in the campaign-local `notebooks/` directory.

```{julia}
campaign_dir = normpath(joinpath(@__DIR__, ".."))
working_data_path = joinpath(campaign_dir, "interim", "working_values.csv")
geometry_path = joinpath(campaign_dir, "calibration_geometry.yaml")
tables_dir = joinpath(campaign_dir, "tables")
figures_dir = joinpath(campaign_dir, "figures")

mkpath(tables_dir)
mkpath(figures_dir)
```

# Load reconciled observations

```{julia}
observations = CSV.read(working_data_path, DataFrame)

required_columns = [
    "observation_id",
    "observer_id",
    "instrument",
    "reference_target_id",
    "angle_deg",
    "observed_time_utc",
]

missing_columns = setdiff(required_columns, names(observations))
isempty(missing_columns) || error("Missing required columns: $(join(missing_columns, ", "))")

nrow(observations)
```

```{julia}
first(observations, 10)
```

# Load calibration geometry

```{julia}
geometry = YAML.load_file(geometry_path)

horizontal_distance_in = Float64(geometry["geometry"]["horizontal_distance"]["value"])
target_records = geometry["geometry"]["reference_targets"]

target_geometry = DataFrame(
    reference_target_id = String[],
    vertical_offset_in = Float64[],
)

for target in target_records
    push!(target_geometry, (
        String(target["reference_target_id"]),
        Float64(target["vertical_offset"]["value"]),
    ))
end

target_geometry.ideal_angle_deg = atand.(
    target_geometry.vertical_offset_in ./ horizontal_distance_in
)

target_geometry
```

# Derive ideal angles and residuals

Residuals are defined as:

$$
\text{residual}
=
\text{observed angle}
-
\text{ideal angle}
$$
Positive residuals indicate that the quadrant reading exceeded the angle implied by the calibration geometry.

```{julia}
analysis_data = leftjoin(
    observations,
    target_geometry,
    on = :reference_target_id,
)

any(ismissing, analysis_data.ideal_angle_deg) &&
    error("At least one observation has no matching calibration target geometry.")

analysis_data.residual_deg = analysis_data.angle_deg .- analysis_data.ideal_angle_deg
analysis_data.abs_residual_deg = abs.(analysis_data.residual_deg)

# Diagnostic flag only; no values are changed or removed.
analysis_data.review_flag = analysis_data.abs_residual_deg .> 5.0

CSV.write(joinpath(tables_dir, "quadrant-calibration-observations.csv"), analysis_data)
first(analysis_data, 12)
```

# Data-integrity review

The following table surfaces observations with absolute residuals greater than 5 degrees. A flag is not a correction and does not establish that an observation is erroneous.

```{julia}
flagged = filter(:review_flag => identity, analysis_data)
flagged
```

# Target-level summary

```{julia}
summary_table = combine(
    groupby(analysis_data, :reference_target_id),
    nrow => :n,
    :vertical_offset_in => first => :vertical_offset_in,
    :ideal_angle_deg => first => :ideal_angle_deg,
    :angle_deg => mean => :mean_observed_deg,
    :angle_deg => std => :sd_observed_deg,
    :angle_deg => minimum => :min_observed_deg,
    :angle_deg => maximum => :max_observed_deg,
    :residual_deg => mean => :mean_residual_deg,
    :residual_deg => std => :sd_residual_deg,
    :abs_residual_deg => mean => :mean_absolute_residual_deg,
)

sort!(summary_table, :vertical_offset_in)
CSV.write(joinpath(tables_dir, "quadrant-calibration-summary.csv"), summary_table)
summary_table
```

# Overall summary

```{julia}
overall_summary = DataFrame(
    statistic = [
        "observations",
        "mean residual (deg)",
        "residual SD (deg)",
        "mean absolute residual (deg)",
        "maximum absolute residual (deg)",
    ],
    value = [
        nrow(analysis_data),
        mean(analysis_data.residual_deg),
        std(analysis_data.residual_deg),
        mean(analysis_data.abs_residual_deg),
        maximum(analysis_data.abs_residual_deg),
    ],
)

CSV.write(joinpath(tables_dir, "quadrant-calibration-overall-summary.csv"), overall_summary)
overall_summary
```

# Diagnostic figures

## Observed and ideal angles

```{julia}
fig_observed = Figure(size = (800, 520))
ax_observed = Axis(
    fig_observed[1, 1],
    xlabel = "Ideal angle (degrees)",
    ylabel = "Observed angle (degrees)",
    title = "Quadrant readings versus calibration geometry",
)

scatter!(ax_observed, analysis_data.ideal_angle_deg, analysis_data.angle_deg)
range_min = min(minimum(analysis_data.ideal_angle_deg), minimum(analysis_data.angle_deg))
range_max = max(maximum(analysis_data.ideal_angle_deg), maximum(analysis_data.angle_deg))
lines!(ax_observed, [range_min, range_max], [range_min, range_max])

save(joinpath(figures_dir, "observed-vs-ideal.png"), fig_observed)
fig_observed
```

## Residual by target

```{julia}
target_order = summary_table.reference_target_id
x_lookup = Dict(target => i for (i, target) in enumerate(target_order))
x_values = [x_lookup[target] for target in analysis_data.reference_target_id]

fig_residual = Figure(size = (900, 520))
ax_residual = Axis(
    fig_residual[1, 1],
    xlabel = "Reference target",
    ylabel = "Residual (degrees)",
    title = "Residuals by calibration target",
    xticks = (1:length(target_order), target_order),
)

scatter!(ax_residual, x_values, analysis_data.residual_deg)
hlines!(ax_residual, [0.0])

save(joinpath(figures_dir, "residuals-by-target.png"), fig_residual)
fig_residual
```

## Mean observed angle with repeatability

```{julia}
fig_summary = Figure(size = (800, 520))
ax_summary = Axis(
    fig_summary[1, 1],
    xlabel = "Ideal angle (degrees)",
    ylabel = "Mean observed angle (degrees)",
    title = "Target means and within-target variation",
)

errorbars!(
    ax_summary,
    summary_table.ideal_angle_deg,
    summary_table.mean_observed_deg,
    summary_table.sd_observed_deg,
)
scatter!(
    ax_summary,
    summary_table.ideal_angle_deg,
    summary_table.mean_observed_deg,
)

summary_min = min(minimum(summary_table.ideal_angle_deg), minimum(summary_table.mean_observed_deg))
summary_max = max(maximum(summary_table.ideal_angle_deg), maximum(summary_table.mean_observed_deg))
lines!(ax_summary, [summary_min, summary_max], [summary_min, summary_max])

save(joinpath(figures_dir, "target-means-vs-ideal.png"), fig_summary)
fig_summary
```

# Initial interpretation

The 0° target was measured accurately, while all elevated targets showed a similar negative residual. The offset did not increase appreciably with target angle, and within-target scatter remained broadly stable. This pattern argues against a simple quadrant zero-point error and instead suggests a systematic change introduced when the observer sighted upward. A plausible mechanism is displacement of the effective eye position caused by head tilt or altered body posture relative to the short-range calibration geometry. Because this geometric effect depends on the proximity of the target, it should be much smaller for astronomical objects at effectively infinite distance, although posture-related handling effects may still require evaluation.
